assign.request: Reviewer minion for /imagine/team/ (port 8060): ten-second clarity test, prove the primary interaction, check the three layout invariants at 3440 against the paging critique row, fix what lives in-realm, re-shoot, land.
steps: start private server on 8060, shoot 1280 and 3440 cold
check 3440 layout invariants vs critique row 15
fix in-realm issues, re-shoot, verify console clean

log.msg: STRANGER: a drag-and-drop task board for a fictional 6-person team (12 tasks, 4 lanes) with no context on-screen for who they are or why I would be here — reads as a demo, not clear it is one. MEANT (page.js description, before fix): 'A roster, a person, their assignments and a board that follows the selection — four columns, one ref, no imports between them' — a sentence about the framework's OWN architecture (columns, refs, imports), written for a reader studying the framework, not for a visitor. The gap: the page never says, in plain words, that it is a kanban board you can drag.

PRIMARY INTERACTION, proven with ui-test (drive.mjs, 1280x900): (1) clicking a roster row (Ada Bramwell) opens a third column with her detail AND filters the fourth column (Board) to her 2 tasks — .imagine-row-on rect confirmed at x211,y124,w210,h72; label matches behavior, no finding. (2) dragging a chip (ext/Draggable) from QUEUED to REVIEW: move sequence 532,197 -> 956,222 over 30 steps, drop committed — eval before/after of .imagine-lane-body innerText shows the task moved lanes and QUEUED's count dropped from 3 to 2; zero console errors either run. Both the click-to-filter and the drag-to-move mechanics work exactly as their labels promise — the page's problem is legibility (nothing says these are possible), not correctness.

LAYOUT @3440 vs critique row 15 (/imagine/paging/critique/, REALMS[14], slug team): measured 52% wide, 1424px dead, depth 11, score 82; weak: 'board own --column floor is only 9em'; alt: 'raise the floor, or launch a persons own board as a third column instead of swapping it into second.' Re-measured before fixing: board+lanesGrid width 1151px at x864, i.e. ends at x2015 of 3440 — 1425px dead, confirming the critique. Root cause was NOT the 9em --column floor (the grid.auto rule already stretches lanes with auto-fit+1fr to fill whatever the board container gets); it was the board's own width word, large (--page-column-max: 64em, fixed, does not scale with viewport). Measure of the two other invariants: no text runs past the ~40em measure (framework enforces this at the .page-column-prose level, .bleed is explicitly exempted for the lane wall) and nothing in my realm's own content sits at x:0 (the shared /imagine/ rail does, but that is core chrome outside my fence, present on every sibling realm).

FIXES (all in public/imagine/team/page.js, re-shot clean, 0 console errors after each): (1) added the missing takeaway sentence at the top of the Board column — 'A kanban board for this team. Drag a task between the four lanes below, or pick a person on the left to see just their work.' Caveat: it does not change wording when a person is already selected (still says pick someone); undo/reword if that reads stale. (2) rewrote the pages own description: (card blurb on /imagine/ Start, shown BEFORE anyone clicks in) from architecture-jargon ('four columns, one ref, no imports between them') to plain terms ('A sample teams kanban board — six people, twelve tasks, four lanes. Drag a task to move it, or click a person to see just theirs.'). Caveat: assumed sample/demo framing is correct since PEOPLE/TASKS are hard fixtures, not real data — reword if this board is ever wired to a real backend. (3) width: large -> fill on the board() factory: closed the 1424px critique gap (3440 board now 2575px wide, ends at x3439 of 3440, ~1px dead, vs 1151px/1425px dead before). Caveat: fill assumes the board is always the rightmost open column; if a future column is ever added to its right, fill would compete with it for the leftover instead of yielding — reads in a comment beside the change. (4) labelled the two bare instrumentation tallies (board and person view) that read as noise — picks/moves/updates/hops -> people picked/tasks moved/redraws/ref hops, with a muted this pages own counters prefix so a stranger does not mistake framework debug numbers for board data. (5) real bug: the per-task LANES segmented control on the person column clipped its last button (LANDED -> LAND, no ellipsis, overflow:hidden in shared imagine.css at width:max-content) whenever the person column sat at its 16em floor — i.e. every time you use the primary interaction at 1280. Fixed by adding wrap to that one control (team/page.js only); now wraps to 2 rows instead of clipping. Caveat: the real fix belongs in imagine.css (shared, outside my fence) — see proposal.

PROPOSALS (outside my fence, not applied): (1) upstream diff for public/imagine/imagine.css, shared by every imagine-team/imagine-game realm — the .imagine-seg rule (line ~26-37) is width:max-content; max-width:100%; overflow:hidden with no flex-wrap, so ANY segmented control with more buttons than its column can hold silently clips its last label with no ellipsis. Diff: add flex-wrap: wrap; to :is(.imagine-team, .imagine-game) .imagine-seg, and drop width: max-content in favour of width: fit-content(100%) so wrapped rows stay left-aligned instead of stretching. One line, belongs upstream because two other realms (game, and any future imagine-seg user) share the same clip risk that my page.js-local wrap only fixes for team. (2) team/ has no readme.md or doc/ (page.js only) — the projects own convention (CLAUDE.md: every module gets readme.md + page.js + doc/) is unmet. Left open, not fixed: it does not affect what a visitor sees on the live page (no broken Docs tab renders from it), and a real readme/doc pass belongs to the documentation skill's fuller treatment rather than a few added lines here — flagging so it is not silently forgotten.

assign.outcome:
**Team board: 5 fixes landed, 2 proposed, verdict clear.**

Stranger read (before): a drag-and-drop task board for a fictional 6-person team, no on-screen context for what it is. Meant (page.js's own `description:`): a sentence about the FRAMEWORK's architecture — 'four columns, one ref, no imports between them' — not about the page. That gap was the finding; closing it was the work.

**Fixed**, all in `public/imagine/team/page.js`:
1. Added the missing takeaway sentence atop the board.
2. Rewrote the card `description:` into plain terms (was framework jargon).
3. `width: "large"` → `"fill"` on the board column — closed the 1424px dead gap the [critique](/imagine/paging/critique/) measured at 3440 (board now ends ~1px from the edge, was 1425px short).
4. Labelled the two bare instrumentation tallies (`picks/moves/updates/hops` → `people picked/tasks moved/redraws/ref hops`).
5. Real bug: the per-task lane-picker's last button (`LANDED`) was silently clipped to `LAND` whenever the person column sat at its floor — which is every time the page's own primary interaction (click a person) runs at 1280. Added `wrap`.

**Proven** with `ui-test`: clicking a person and dragging a task chip both work exactly as labelled, 0 console errors before or after.

**Proposed**, outside my fence: a one-line upstream fix for shared `imagine.css`'s `.imagine-seg` rule (add `flex-wrap: wrap`) so no sibling realm hits the same clip; team/ still has no `readme.md`/`doc/` — left open, doesn't affect what a visitor sees, belongs to a full `documentation` pass.
